quote: I don't think I'm in the area.
stewart_read: Customer questions basic eligibility/legitimacy before any rapport; rep resolves quickly by checking service area live.
coaching_implication: Fast, confident resolution worked here — good model for other reps facing early service-area doubt.

quote: Duke Power company paid for it. So there are any of those around.
stewart_read: Customer references a competitor/utility-funded program; rep gives a thin, uninvestigated dismissal instead of probing what she actually saw.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have genuinely not known and chose not to fabricate — a defensible knowledge-gap response, not fabrication.
coaching_implication: Better move: acknowledge uncertainty and bridge to specialist rather than a flat 'I don't think so,' which could read as dismissive.

quote: let me let me talk with them, and I can I can get back with you?
stewart_read: This is a soft stall/objection disguised as politeness; rep does not concede and instead pivots to a no-commitment quote offer.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read would be that rep should have addressed neighbor comparison directly, but the strategic pivot to 'no decisions needed' bypassed the objection more efficiently.
coaching_implication: This objection-inversion-style pivot worked; worth reinforcing as a repeatable move for stall-type objections.

stewart_read: The interest question was never asked, per verified events, meaning the emotional anchor for the whole pitch is missing.
coaching_implication: Without knowing why she wants solar, the rep has no emotional hook to tie the appointment or text follow-up back to.

stewart_read: Bill captured but never flipped into an emotional utility-villain reframe — rep just logs the number and moves to the next question.
coaching_implication: Rep should have echoed the number back as pain ('that $350 month is exactly what we're trying to eliminate') to build urgency before bill collection.

quote: It says March 24 to March 2026, But I don't this this graph only shows January to December.
stewart_read: Customer is actively engaging with her own usage graph, effectively doing curiosity-creation on herself, but rep doesn't build on it, just reassures the picture 'will work for us.'
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have deprioritized this to keep the call moving toward booking, a reasonable time-management call given the appointment was close.
coaching_implication: A quick 'see how it spikes in summer? that's exactly what we design around' would have used her own engagement as a hook.

quote: How long have you guys been in business?
stewart_read: Customer's unsolicited legitimacy question this late in the call signals she's leaning toward trusting the appointment, not looking for an exit.
coaching_implication: Rep answered directly and added unsolicited credibility ('never been in debt'); good handling, reinforced trust right before booking.
